image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small Bangkok Hospital clinic building, detailed front elevation with a glazed curtain-wall frontage and automatic doors under a shallow projecting entrance canopy, blue and white signage band carrying the Bangkok Hospital wordmark in Thai and English, white composite cladding panels across the upper front, plain warm cream painted side and rear walls in a single flat off-white tone clearly lighter than the background, with a service door and high windows, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: white composite cladding and blue printed sign face at the front, clear curtain-wall glazing, flat warm cream painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless MID-DARK neutral grey (#606060), distinctly darker than every part of the building so the object reads as a clean cut-out against it. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Bangkok Hospital / BDMS. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT (v6, re-assessed). Overall visual fidelity 0.90 -- re-judged against the plate with a matched side-by-side and a front-elevation column scan; the ground floor's share of the elevation (0.41 vs the plate's 0.30) and the unweathered flat wall material are what hold it under 0.92; three of the changes follow the owner's instruction over the plate and are recorded as such. 1212/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries, 2 textures. The plate's -X canopy wrap is the one feature knowingly left out.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 6.00 x 7.00 m (render bounds; v5/v6 raised on the owner's instruction). Cream box capped at 5.45, white block to 6.00 with a 1.27 m return over each side wall from the sign top, canopy nose at z=3.50; the rooftop units (1.20 x 0.90 x 1.10 m) stand on the deck at 5.02 and top out at 5.99 under the envelope, 0.54 m above the parapet. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m on the v6 build.
featureReviews.notes: Re-assessed on v6. The plate's front stack by column scan is 0.31 cladding / 0.16 sign / 0.18 strip zone / 0.05 canopy / 0.30 ground glazing; the build is 0.27 / 0.17 / 0.15 / 0.03 / 0.41 of 6.00 m -- the ground floor is still proportionally taller than the plate's (a 2.1 m door under the plate's canopy implies a ~7.6 m building) and the upper storey shorter, the one open massing residual with the -X canopy wrap, which is not built. Subject bbox aspect 1.208 on the plate against 1.154 rendered at 45/25 (camera not matched, so weak evidence).

featureReviews.evidence: ONE board 7.80 x 1.00 m across the +Z front at y 3.36..4.36, 0.14 m proud: its left half white (#C4C8CE) with blue 'Bangkok Hospital' spanning the full half width and the small Thai name above it, both lines right-justified in their half (v5), its right half #3B7BD8 with the same in white -- one canvas split at u 0.5, one material, one draw call. Front render (review/beauty-000.png) shows the split at the facade centre, both wordmarks legible and the Thai line above each.
featureReviews.notes: Re-assessed on v6: sign share of the elevation 0.17 built against 0.16 on the plate; the plate's Thai name sits small above the right end of the English on both boards and the build now does the same (right-justified). Residuals: one full-width board where the plate has two separate boards (owner's v3 instruction), and the blue lifted to #3B7BD8 from the measured #1C498B for the luma-only silhouette gate.

featureReviews.evidence: Top to bottom: panelled cladding with six joints (4.36..6.00), sign band (3.36..4.36), strip window (2.65..3.34, six bars), canopy slab (2.45..2.65), ground glazing 0.05..2.45 with a transom through its top eighth at 2.08 and the sliding entrance CENTRED under it (jambs -0.75..0.75, meeting stile, NO mid rail) and THREE glazing sections each side (mullions -2.83, -1.79, 1.79, 2.83). On +X: the upper window (2.72..4.32, rising to the sign top under the white return) with a centre mullion only, the lower window floor-to-head (0.05..2.45) with a centre mullion and a transom at 2.08, and the service door inset behind a proud aluminium surround under a 0.15 m hood, with a small lever handle (review/beauty-045.png).
featureReviews.notes: Re-assessed on v6 against the side-by-side: every element the plate shows on the front and the +X wall is present in the same order and place -- transom through the top of the ground glazing, rail-free sliding door, strip window, sign, panelled cladding with the white top returning over both side walls, floor-to-head lower side window with a high transom, tall upper side window to the sign top, inset door with hood and handle, two units standing clear of the parapet. Residuals: door centred where the plate has it left of centre (owner's instruction); the plate's upper side window is proportionally a little wider; exterior shell, no interior.

featureReviews.evidence: A 0.20 m thick slab projecting 0.58 m off the block face to z=3.50, the full 8.00 m width, with a visible edge fascia at every turntable azimuth.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged from v2. The -X wrap is not built (see overall-silhouette).
